best_for: Script authors and module maintainers who want to test the next PowerShell release on Windows or Mac before it ships, without touching their stable install.

points.title: Runs beside stable PowerShell
points.text: Previews install to a separate `7-preview` folder and start with `pwsh-preview`, so your regular `pwsh` stays as it is. A newer preview replaces the older preview.

points.title: Not for production
points.text: Microsoft says previews can contain breaking changes and bugs, and they are not officially supported. Use them to test scripts and modules, then report problems on GitHub.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Like stable PowerShell, the preview is MIT-licensed and built on .NET.

points.title: Windows packages are MSIX
points.text: The Windows builds here are MSIX packages for x64, x86 and Arm64, needing Windows 10 version 1809 (build 17763) or later. MSIX installs are per user and do not accept incoming WSMan remoting or settings that write to `$PSHOME`.

points.title: Mac packages for both chips
points.text: macOS gets .pkg installers for Intel and Apple silicon, placed under `/usr/local/microsoft/powershell/7-preview/`. Homebrew users can install the `powershell@preview` cask instead.

points.title: Two platforms, two numbering styles
points.text: The newest Windows entry is 7.7.5.0, the MSIX package number, while macOS shows 7.7.0-rc.1. The Windows listing keeps 49 versions; macOS lists only the current preview.
